exact_statement: For every fixed integer d >= 3, every N-point subset of R^d determines N^(2/d-o(1)) distinct distances as N tends to infinity.
scope_notes: The public statement and sole success condition are copied from the frozen round-five campaign.

Round six does not modify frozen round five.  It generalizes only the displayed formal relative-unit matrix from three rows to m rows and separately audits whether that matrix is realized by an actual power-large paired-positive common-X block.

A formal all-m rank, kernel, or Smith theorem is another local normal form unless the real-block incidence, extra-row, variable, occurrence-mass, fibre, full-target and stability interfaces are all proved.
Promotion requires a rigorous dimension-three exponent strictly greater than 3/5; no finite matrix experiment or conditional matrix bridge qualifies.
